title: Earth & Space
description: Grade 5 Science: Earth and space — the solar system, the planets, stars and constellations, gravity in space, and space exploration including India's missions.

topics.title: The Solar System
topics.concept:
The Solar System is the Sun and everything that travels around it. The Sun's gravity holds it all together.

  • ☀️ The Sun — a star — sits at the centre.
  • 🪐 Eight planets travel around the Sun, each on its own path called an orbit.
  • 🌙 Many planets have moons circling them.
  • ☄️ There are also smaller rocks — asteroids and comets.

recap: The Solar System is the Sun and all that orbits it.
Eight planets orbit the Sun; the Sun's gravity holds them.
There are also moons, asteroids and comets.

wonder.text: Our Earth is one small ball whirling around the Sun, along with seven other worlds. What holds this giant space family together?

qa.q: What keeps the planets going around the Sun?
qa.a: The Sun's gravity! Its strong pull keeps all the planets moving around it in their orbits, instead of drifting off into deep space.
An orbit is the path an object takes around another in space. Each planet travels its own oval orbit around the Sun, again and again.

topics.title: The Planets
topics.concept:
The eight planets, in order from the Sun, are: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

  • ☿️ Mercury — closest to the Sun and very hot.
  • 🌍 Earth — the only planet known to have life.
  • 🔴 Mars — the 'red planet', a cold desert world.
  • 🪐 Jupiter — the biggest planet; Saturn has bright rings.

A fun way to remember the order: 'My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Names'!

recap: Eight planets orbit the Sun, from Mercury to Neptune.
Earth is the only planet known to have life.
Mars is the red planet; Jupiter is the biggest; Saturn has rings.

wonder.text: One planet is a baking-hot rock, another is a giant ball of gas, and one has beautiful rings. How are the eight planets so different?

qa.q: Why is Mars called the red planet?
qa.a: Mars looks red because its soil is full of rusty iron dust. From far away, all that reddish dust gives the whole planet a red colour.
Jupiter is the biggest — so huge that all the other planets could fit inside it! It is a giant ball of gas with a famous Great Red Spot, a giant storm.

topics.title: Stars and Constellations
topics.concept:
Stars are giant balls of hot, glowing gas — just like our Sun. They look like tiny dots only because they are unbelievably far away.

  • ⭐ Stars make their own light; planets and moons do not.
  • 🌌 Groups of stars that form a pattern or picture are called constellations (like the Saptarishi / Big Dipper).
  • 🧭 Long ago, sailors used stars to find their way at night.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="180" fill="#0b1437"/><g fill="#ffffff"><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="1.5"/><circle cx="260" cy="36" r="1.5"/><circle cx="120" cy="150" r="1.5"/><circle cx="270" cy="140" r="1.5"/></g><g fill="#ffe98a"><circle cx="70" cy="60" r="4"/><circle cx="110" cy="48" r="4"/><circle cx="150" cy="66" r="4"/><circle cx="186" cy="58" r="4"/><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="4"/><circle cx="120" cy="130" r="4"/><circle cx="96" cy="150" r="4"/></g><polyline points="70,60 110,48 150,66 186,58 150,110 120,130 96,150" fill="none" stroke="#6f7db0" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="150" y="26" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#cfd6ff" text-anchor="middle">A constellation</text></svg>
recap: Stars are huge balls of hot, glowing gas, like the Sun.
They look tiny because they are very far away.
A pattern of stars is called a constellation.

wonder.text: The night sky is full of twinkling dots. Some seem to make pictures. What are stars, really?

qa.a: Starlight travels a huge distance and passes through our moving air before reaching us. The air bends the light a little this way and that, making the star seem to twinkle.
A constellation is a group of stars that seem to make a shape or picture in the sky, like a hunter or a bear. People named them long ago to find their way and tell stories.

topics.title: Gravity and Space
topics.concept:
Gravity is a pulling force. Earth's gravity pulls everything down towards the ground and keeps us from floating away.

  • 🌍 Earth's gravity gives us weight and keeps the air and oceans in place.
  • ☀️ The Sun's gravity holds the planets in their orbits.
  • 🌙 The Moon's gravity is weaker, so astronauts can take giant bounces there!

Far out in space, away from Earth, gravity is very weak — so astronauts float.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 240 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="240" height="200" fill="#0b1437"/><circle cx="120" cy="150" r="70" fill="#3f86d6"/><path d="M70 120 A70 70 0 0 1 174 116 Q140 132 110 124 Q86 118 70 120 Z" fill="#3fa86a"/><circle cx="150" cy="40" r="12" fill="#ff5a5a"/><path d="M150 18 q6 -8 14 -6" stroke="#2BCB8B" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/><g stroke="#FFC93C" stroke-width="4" marker-end="url(#gr)"><line x1="150" y1="56" x2="150" y2="84"/></g><defs><marker id="gr" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#FFC93C"/></marker></defs><text x="176" y="74" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#ffe08a">Gravity pulls down</text></svg>
recap: Gravity is a pulling force; Earth's gravity pulls things down.
The Sun's gravity keeps planets in orbit.
Far from Earth, gravity is weak, so astronauts float.

wonder.text: On Earth, everything you drop falls down. But astronauts in space float around. Where did gravity go?

qa.q: Why do astronauts float in a spaceship?
qa.a: A spaceship and everything in it are falling around the Earth together, so things feel weightless and float. Far from Earth, gravity's pull is also much weaker.

qa.q: Would I weigh the same on the Moon?
qa.a: No! The Moon's gravity is much weaker than Earth's — about one-sixth. So on the Moon you would weigh much less and could jump super high!

topics.title: Exploring Space
topics.concept:
People explore space using powerful rockets, satellites and robot space probes.

  • 🚀 Rockets are powerful enough to escape Earth's gravity.
  • 🛰️ Satellites circle Earth to help with TV, phones, weather and maps.
  • 👨‍🚀 Astronauts have walked on the Moon and live on the Space Station.
  • 🇮🇳 India's ISRO sent Chandrayaan to the Moon and Mangalyaan to Mars — and India was the first country to reach Mars on its very first try!

recap: We explore space with rockets, satellites and probes.
Satellites help with TV, phones, weather and maps.
India's ISRO reached the Moon (Chandrayaan) and Mars (Mangalyaan).

wonder.text: How do humans reach the Moon and send robots to Mars, millions of kilometres away?

qa.q: What does a satellite do for us?
qa.a: Satellites circling Earth help us in daily life — they carry TV and phone signals, take weather pictures, and power the maps that show us the way.

qa.q: What is India famous for in space?
qa.a: India's space agency, ISRO, landed Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon's south pole and sent Mangalyaan to Mars on its first attempt — making India a proud space explorer!

questions.q: At the centre of the Solar System is the…
questions.explanation: The Sun is at the centre, with planets orbiting around it.

questions.q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: There are eight planets, from Mercury to Neptune.

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explanation: We live on Earth — the only planet known to have life.

options: Huge balls of hot glowing gas
questions.explanation: Stars are huge balls of hot, glowing gas, like the Sun.

questions.q: The force that pulls things down to Earth is…
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls everything down towards the Earth.

questions.q: India's mission that reached Mars is called…
questions.explanation: Mangalyaan was India's mission to Mars; Chandrayaan went to the Moon.

questions.q: What keeps the planets moving around the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun's gravity holds the planets in their orbits.

questions.q: Why do stars look like tiny dots?
questions.explanation: Stars are huge but so far away that they look like tiny dots.

questions.q: Why is Mars called the red planet?
options: Its soil is full of rusty red dust
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because of the rusty iron dust covering it.

questions.q: Why do astronauts float far out in space?
options: Gravity's pull is very weak far from Earth
questions.explanation: Far from Earth, gravity is very weak, so astronauts float.

questions.q: Put the planets in order from the Sun: Earth, Mercury, Mars, Venus.
questions.explanation: From the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
